issues.body: The new GREEN_DROP_REASONS arm relies entirely on verdict_is_still_for_this_tree(), but verdict_state() timestamps a `committed` event with `committer.date` (falling back to `author.date`). Those are commit metadata, not the time the commit entered the PR. If review:pass is granted and an old-dated commit is subsequently pushed (for example by cherry-picking or preserving dates), `head_moved_at` remains earlier than `review_pass_at`; a later QUEUE_CLEARED/ROLL_BACK then preserves the stale verdict and calls `gh pr merge --auto`. The new tests hand-build chronological dates and therefore do not exercise this failure. This is load-bearing because this arm intentionally requires no watchdog marker or group-head binding.
issues.fix_hint: Bind the verdict to the actual reviewed head SHA, or derive post-grant movement from timeline event ordering / an event occurrence timestamp rather than commit-authored metadata. Add an end-to-end timeline test where the `labeled` event precedes a `committed` event whose committer/author date predates the label, and assert that QUEUE_CLEARED/ROLL_BACK demotes instead of preserving.
issues.title: Queue-drop preservation can carry a verdict across an unreviewed head change

verdict.summary: The new markerless preserve route is not safely bound to the reviewed tree. Its sole tree-integrity guard derives ordinary commit movement from the commit's author/committer date, rather than when that commit was added to the PR. A post-approval push of an old-dated commit can therefore pass the guard and have review:pass preserved and the PR automatically re-armed on QUEUE_CLEARED/ROLL_BACK. The tests cover only conveniently ordered timestamps and miss this real timeline case.
